a blue sky that seemed like it would become even bluer.

rows.en: Taichi Physics. A class of observer problem that occurs within certain stable situations. Those who can see, see; those who cannot remain unable to see, and the assigned property manifests physically. A major change in the situation will usually clear the property.

I prayed with all my heart.

rows.jp: 「結論から言うとー、君は引き金を引いていい。その権利があるよ、霧には」
rows.en: “I’ll say this first: you can pull that trigger. You have that right, Kiri.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If at the conclusion, and only then, you pull the trigger then it's fine. That's a privilege you have, Kiri."
ghs.assessment: Taichi prefaces his conclusion and says Kiri may pull the trigger because she has that right. The English invents a condition that she may fire only at the conclusion.
ghs.remedy: To give you the conclusion first: you may pull the trigger.

highlights.text: If at the conclusion, and only then, you pull the trigger then it's fine.

rows.jp: 俺は今また、霧を食べようとしているのだから。
rows.en: Even now, I was trying to devour Kiri again.

ghs.en: for I, still, do want to devour Kiri.

rows.jp: さあ霧、俺は命を賭けたぞ。
rows.en: There, Kiri. I’ve put my life on the line.

ghs.en: Well then, Kiri, I'm putting my life at stake.

rows.en: Come at me with everything you have, junior.

ghs.en: Come at me with full force, my Kouhai.
Taichi: "The cause of Yutaka's death was suicide."
Taichi: "But the cause of that was me."
We sink into a silence without end.
Taichi: "It's a tale that'll run long though."

rows.jp: 「それで、わたしを解放してください」

ghs.en: Kiri: "And with that, please set me free."

rows.en: Her heart would have to settle on one or the other.

ghs.en: which of the two will we end at?

rows.jp: 霧の心は、いずれかしか受けつけないのだろう。
rows.en: It could probably accept no state between them.

ghs.en: Kiri's mind will likely accept only either of these.

rows.jp: 唾液で喉を潤して、俺は話しはじめた。
rows.en: I swallowed to wet my throat and began to speak.

ghs.en: Wetting my throat with saliva, I began to speak.

rows.jp: 「支倉って家があったんだ、昔」
rows.en: “There used to be a family called the Hasekuras.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There was this family called the Hasekuras, long ago."

rows.jp: 「大きな家でさ。洋風で。桐原の家を十倍くらい大きくしたような」
rows.en: “They had a huge Western-style house—about ten times the size of the Kiriharas’.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "They had a big house. Western style. So big it was about ten times Kirihara's house."

rows.jp: 「俺は……幼い頃に母親を亡くして、そこに引き取られた」
rows.en: “When I was little... my mother died, and I was taken in there.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was... well, when I was a child my mother passed, and I was taken into their custody."

rows.jp: 「そこに住み込みで働く、母親の遠縁にあたる管理人夫妻にね」
rows.en: “By the live-in caretakers, a married couple distantly related to her.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was a live-in worker there, for a manager and his wife who were distant relatives of mother's."
ghs.assessment: The live-in workers were the caretaker couple, distant relatives of Taichi's mother, who took him in. The English wrongly makes Taichi the worker.
ghs.remedy: by the caretaker couple who lived and worked there and were distant relatives of my mother

highlights.text: I was a live-in worker there

rows.en: “The household had customs that went back a long way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It was a family with old customs, you know."

rows.jp: 「下働きの子供は、やっぱり下働きだった」
rows.en: “A servant’s child was expected to serve too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The children of servants were made servants, seriously."

rows.jp: 「俺は子供だったから、家の子供たちの遊び相手みたいな役割だった」
rows.en: “I was a kid, so I more or less served as a playmate for the family’s children.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was just a child, therefore, my duty was to be sort of a playmate for the children of the family."

rows.jp: 「曜子ちゃんはそこの末娘だった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan was the youngest girl there."
